fixtures.label: Three orders, one organization — the delivery leg
fixtures.description:
The family's FIRST fixture, covering what the family exists for: a CROSS-ORDER sheet. Address `organization:s7WXepzsnaTbaKF0Et1T:all:delivery`, which pins the `<kind>:<uid>:<gate>:<leg>` grammar (api-cloudrun#824) on its `organization` arm. Re-captured 2026-09-09: orders 970, 1013 and 1014 across three destinations, 423 units.

🔴 THIS FAMILY'S SOURCE IS OPEN WORK, SO THE ADDRESS IS STABLE AND THE DOCUMENT IS NOT. A delivery sheet holds the bookings still awaiting delivery, so an order leaves it the moment its units go `out`. RE-POINTED here: the previous source (`organization:nTpq3YIY4cth5todd4PV`, orders 964 + 1020) had gone out and returned a ONE-order sheet, which is not this fixture's shape. Check the sheet is still cross-order before blessing its golden — a decayed source degrades silently into a document that renders fine and covers nothing.

1. THE GROUP HEADINGS, across all three orders — what `buildPackingListForLeg` (core#80, beta.326) exists to keep. The bug it fixed was SILENT: `groupByDestination` strips dividers while `buildPackingList` walks for the last `group` row it passed, so composing them returned null for every heading. The grid rendered and the headings a picker navigates by were absent. Only a rendered sheet catches it.

2. RENTAL AND SALE TOGETHER — the delivery leg's defining property, carried by order 1013's six `sale` lines beside its rentals. Delivery admits both; collection is rental only, because a sale does not come back. A collection-leg fixture is NOT a near-duplicate.

3. A COMPLETE DOCUMENT. `order_count` is 3 and the fold returns 3 with `next_cursor: null`, so `orders.length === order_count` holds — the template REFUSES a short document.

4. THREE DESTINATIONS under gate `all`, mixing customer-collecting and crew legs.

⚠️ NOT small any more, and that claim is dropped rather than quietly kept: at 423 units this golden no longer reads in one view. Its job is the cross-order shape.

fixtures.label: The collection leg — rental only
fixtures.description:
The COLLECTION leg, and the family's only fixture for it: before it, half of what this family renders was compared against nothing while `visual-diff` passed (templates#226). `PickSheet.leg` is DATA, not a render param, so no param state can reach this rendering. Partner: `multi-order-delivery`.

Address `order:YWzMc44iBt6bFWPrci0f:all:collection` — prod order 1007. ⭐ RE-POINTED 2026-09-09 from `organization:kmyrrrizBnD4J2ADzThK:all:collection`: an organization-scoped sheet holds whatever is open at that scope TODAY, and a second order had joined it, so that address no longer named a single-order sheet. The degenerate `order` scope (api-cloudrun#821) names one order by construction, so the defining property cannot decay away. Its sibling covers the `organization` arm.

Three load-bearing branches, unrendered before it: `legKey` selects `packing_list_collection`; `legLabel` sets the heading to "Packing List — Collection"; the returns column is driven by `orderHasRentals`.

⭐ RENTAL ONLY, not by chance — the leg's defining property. A sale does not come back; the delivery partner deliberately carries a `sale` line beside its rentals.

Its source has real COMPONENTS (five products under each of two Pop Up Tents, `path` four deep), but they are all zero_priced, so at the family default (`hide_zero_priced_components: true`) they are hidden and the tents render alone. It therefore pins nothing about indentation: since 2026-10-12 the sheet takes the quote and invoice indent rules (banners flush, components 1em per level), and those are rendered by `kit-components-shown` and `multi-order-delivery`.

COMPLETE: `order_count` is 1 and the fold returns 1 with `next_cursor: null`, so the `orders.length === order_count` assertion holds.

⭐ Same prod order as the receipt family's `checkout-no-reference` — that is these tents going out, this is collecting them back. ⚠️ `scope.name` is filler here — core#99.

fixtures.label: Kit with zero-priced components, shown
fixtures.description: The `hide_zero_priced_components: false` half of a control pair, and the only fixture rendering that state (the family default is true). Address `order:h2O0vI0LUb0OyBWi0gcR:all:delivery` (prod order 1064), captured 2026-10-12 after the zero_priced backfill, so its kit carries real flags: two components zero_priced true and one zero_priced false, the arm that must STAY when the param hides the rest. Its sibling `kit-components-hidden` is the SAME capture at true, so the diff between the two goldens is the param's effect alone: re-capture both together or the pair stops being a control. Delivery leg on an order scope, so the shape cannot decay; the contents can once the order goes out, so check the kit rows survive before blessing.

fixtures.label: Kit with zero-priced components, hidden
fixtures.description: The `hide_zero_priced_components: true` state (the family default) on a kit with real flags. SAME capture as `kit-components-shown` (prod order 1064, delivery leg, 2026-10-12), so the two goldens differ only by the param: the two zero_priced components drop, and the zero_priced false component stays under its kit, which is the row the predicate must not catch. Stated explicitly rather than left to the default so the pair stays a control if the default ever moves. Re-capture together with `kit-components-shown` or not at all.

fixtures.label: Serialized units out — the assigned Units line
fixtures.description: The only fixture rendering the ASSIGNED arm of the serialized-row `Units:` line (templates#473/#474): its Walkie Talkie booking carries 85 named units out, 1001–1087 with two gaps (1018, 1071), so the line must read `Units: Out 1001–1017, 1019–1070, 1072–1087` — three ranges, which is what pins the range-folding and the gap handling rather than one unbroken run. Every other fixture renders only `Units: unassigned` (the Walkie Talkie in `kit-components-shown` / `kit-components-hidden`). Address `order:0Vf8CyXIqyggYRKt0MVF:all:collection` — prod order 1069, captured 2026-10-21 while every unit was out. COLLECTION leg on an order scope on purpose: a delivery sheet drops a booking once its units go out, so only the collection leg still holds them, and the `order` scope cannot gain a second order. The SOURCE decays the day the units return (collection due 2026-10-22), so a re-capture after that will NOT reproduce this shape — check the Units line before blessing a re-capture. Only the `out` state is covered: prod held 0 bookings with units prepped at capture, so `Units: Prepped …` is still rendered by no fixture. Incidental, not its job: the kit's two zero_priced components hide at the family default, the zero_priced false Walkie Case stays, and the Surveillance Kit carries 11 lost beside 64 out.
